title: r1 W1 only half-folded: flush call-site ordering (trigger before pending clear) is still unpinned, while code/test comments now claim it is unit-pinned
detail: Moving `flush_maybe_duck(a)` after `a.pending = {}` in audio_flush silently kills all ducking (counts already zeroed) and every one of the 18 tests stays green — the exact r1 W1 ordering risk now carries a false 'unit-pinned' assurance, which is worse than unpinned.
recommended_fix: Fold the pending clear into flush_maybe_duck itself (or a flush_finish proc called unconditionally by audio_flush) so the before-clear ordering is enforced by construction inside the tested proc; fix the comments to match what is actually pinned.

title: Build script's decode-compare mismatch only prints and exits 0 — after the fresh encode has already overwritten the committed OGG
evidence:
`], check=True, timeout=600)  # r1 review: a hung ffmpeg must not block forever` (encode writes OUT_OGG in place), then `if fresh_pcm_sha == committed_pcm_sha:
        print("audio-identity vs the committed artifact: MATCH")
    else:
        print("audio-identity vs the committed artifact: DIFFERS — the loop contract "
              "changed; re-derive A/B/XF deliberately")` — every other guard in the script uses `raise SystemExit(...)` (e.g. `raise SystemExit(f"vault WAV sha256 mismatch:...")`).
detail: On the one check that detects a changed loop contract, the script leaves a modified assets/audio/ambience_loop.ogg in the tree and returns success — inconsistent with the script's own fail-loud guard discipline and the repo's errors-must-surface rule; easy to miss in a scroll of output.
recommended_fix: Encode to a temp path, compare decoded PCM, and only move over OUT_OGG on match (or SystemExit on DIFFERS), matching the script's other guards.

title: Committed reproducibility script hard-codes a developer-machine absolute path for the vault source
evidence: `SRC = "/Users/moses/code/_local-refs/audio/Warm Analog Drift.wav"` — a committed file under tools/ with no env-var/CLI override; the README repeats the same absolute path as the transform's source.
detail: The 'documented, reproducible transform' contract only runs on one machine as committed; any other checkout of the repo (or a future machine of the same user) must edit the script to point at a vault copy, weakening the reproducibility-by-construction goal the r1 B1 fold established.
recommended_fix: Read the vault path from an env var (e.g. PP_VAULT_WAV) or argv with this path as the documented default; keep the sha256 pin unchanged.

title: `paused` parameter (sim-freeze) collides with `bed_paused` field (mute mirror) in the same small API
evidence: `bed_paused:     bool, // the mute mirror (the raylib pause/resume's pure twin — asserted headlessly)` vs `bed_update :: proc(a: ^Audio, dt: f32, paused: bool) {` where the call site passes `app.mode == .Paused` (app/main.odin:502).
detail: Two unrelated pause concepts (5.3 sim-freeze soft-lower vs M-key stream pause) share one word one screen apart; a future edit wiring `a.bed_paused` into bed_update's `paused` argument (or vice versa) reads as plausible and inverts the mode level.
recommended_fix: Rename the parameter to `sim_paused` (or the field to `bed_mute_paused`) so the two pause domains are lexically distinct.
